title: Generate built-in RBAC v2 role templates from YAML + CI linting + versioned policy bundle artifacts
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Problem
We need a canonical, reproducible way to define built-in role templates (Org Admin, Security Admin, Read-only Auditor, Deployment Operator, etc.) that is:
- human-editable (reviewable in PRs)
- lintable in CI (to prevent accidental over-privilege or invalid permission strings)
- versioned and publishable as a release artifact consumed by Redwood services (gateway/control plane/console) and Private installer bootstrap.

Today role templates exist as a mix of draft docs and hand-maintained JSON. This is already drifting across Hosted/Dedicated/Private and is causing issues during dogfood/pilots (missing permissions, inconsistent scopes).

Scope
1) Define YAML schema for role templates and bundle metadata.
2) Implement a generator that outputs a versioned “policy bundle” artifact (machine-consumable JSON) from YAML.
3) Add CI linting to enforce invariants:
   - permission naming format per ADR-014
   - no unknown permissions (must exist in permission registry)
   - no deprecated permissions without explicit allowlist/justification comment
   - scopes must be valid (org/project/environment/cluster) and consistent with permission’s allowed scopes
   - no duplicate roles, stable role IDs
   - deterministic output (generator is stable across runs)
4) Add a release process for the generated artifact (tagged version) and document consumption for services.

Non-goals
- Customer-defined custom policy language (ABAC) or arbitrary conditional rules.
- Re-architecting identity; this is purely role template definition + packaging.

Proposed design (high level)
- Source of truth: YAML files under rbac-policy-bundle repo.
  - roles/*.yaml (one role template per file)
  - bundle.yaml (bundle metadata: version, min platform version, changelog pointer)
- Generator produces:
  - dist/policy-bundle.json (all templates + metadata; deterministic ordering)
  - dist/roles/<role_slug>.json (optional split outputs for debugging)
  - dist/checksums.txt (for integrity; used by installer)
- Linter runs as required CI check:
  - schema validation (YAML)
  - semantic validation (permission registry lookup, scope constraints)
  - “least-privilege guardrails” (e.g., role named *Auditor* cannot include write actions unless explicitly annotated)

Acceptance criteria
- [x] YAML schema documented (README) with examples for org-scoped and cluster-scoped roles.
- [x] Generator produces deterministic outputs and includes bundle version.
- [x] CI fails on unknown permissions, invalid scope types, duplicate role IDs, and non-deterministic output.
- [x] Artifact release procedure documented (tag -> CI builds -> upload/release artifact).
- [x] Control plane and private installer can consume the artifact format without manual edits (follow-up adoption tracked separately).

Implementation notes
- Prefer a small, auditable generator (Go) with strict parsing; avoid complex templating.
- “Allowed scopes per permission” will be sourced from the permission registry metadata introduced in redwood PR-28134. The generator/linter should be able to ingest a pinned registry snapshot (or fetch from a versioned file) to keep policy-bundle repo decoupled from the monorepo.
- Output should include:
  - role_id (stable UUID or stable slug-based ID)
  - display_name
  - description
  - default_scopes (if applicable)
  - permissions[] (strings)
  - constraints (e.g., requires_break_glass=false) as a reserved field (even if unused in v2) — keep forward-compatible.

Testing
- Unit tests for:
  - deterministic output given same input
  - linting edge cases: deprecated perms, invalid names, invalid scope
- Golden file tests for dist output to catch accidental diffs.

Rollout plan
- Land generator + linter in rbac-policy-bundle.
- Publish policy-bundle v0.3.0.
- Services adopt the artifact behind feature flag (tracked in ENG-18388 / service-specific tickets).

Links
- GitHub: rbac-policy-bundle PR-184 (generate role templates from YAML)
- GitHub: rbac-policy-bundle PR-201 (add Private deployment operator roles)
- Related: redwood PR-28134 (permission enum/registry)
- Related: Confluence “Role templates and matrix” + permission inventory (for source role definitions)

Open questions (resolved)
- Versioning: Use semver on the policy bundle; services pin a version and allow override via config. Bundle version is independent from Redwood platform version but includes min_platform_version metadata.
- Artifact distribution: GitHub Releases + attached bundle; Private installer can embed a pinned release SHA/version for bootstrap.

Risks
- Drift between permission registry and policy bundle if not pinned. Mitigation: bundle.yaml pins registry_version and CI verifies the referenced registry snapshot.
- Over-privileged templates slipping through. Mitigation: lint rules + required Security Eng review on role template changes (CODEOWNERS).
activity: 2025-02-07 (Jordan Lee): Ticket created after role matrix workshop notes flagged repeated manual edits + drift risk. Proposal: YAML as source-of-truth + generator + linter.

2025-02-11 (Naomi Feldman): +1. Please ensure generated artifact includes human-readable descriptions; Support/CS will reference these in Console role template picker. Also want a stable identifier that can be used in audit logs (“role_template_id”).

2025-02-14 (Marcus Lin): Security requirements: (1) deterministic generation, (2) CI must block unknown permissions and deprecated permissions by default, (3) CODEOWNERS on roles/*.yaml and generator code; require Security review for role template changes that include high-sensitivity permissions (e.g., audit export, key rotation, routing policy edits).

2025-02-18 (Diego Santos): Private needs cluster-scoped templates; ensure schema supports scopeType=cluster and example bindings (org->cluster). Also include checksums for integrity verification during air-gapped installs.

2025-02-24 (Jordan Lee): Implemented first pass generator + schema validation. Added golden file tests and stable ordering. Output contains bundle_version + min_platform_version + role_template_id (slug-based) and permissions list.

2025-03-03 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Confirmed control plane consumer can ingest bundle.json (simple JSON decode). Requested field name alignment with authz decision logging (“policy_bundle_version”). Jordan to rename metadata field to match audit log schema expectations.

2025-03-06 (Jordan Lee): Added semantic lint step: validate permission strings against registry snapshot + validate allowed_scopes. Added failure messages that point to the exact YAML file and permission causing failure.
2025-03-10 (Connor O'Brien): Release process request: tag -> CI artifact -> release notes. Added checklist to repo docs. Target v0.3.0 by 3/14 for pilot accounts.

2025-03-14 (Jordan Lee): PR-184 merged. Published policy bundle v0.3.0 to GitHub Releases with attached policy-bundle.json + checksums. Follow-up PR-201 adding Private operator roles queued; will cut v0.3.1 once merged.
2025-03-21 (Jordan Lee): Marking Done. Next steps tracked elsewhere: service adoption, console template picker wiring, and installer bootstrap pin updates.
